simple.meaning: יָעַף (yâʻaph) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to tire (as if from wearisome flight ).” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 10 times in Judges, Isaiah, Jeremiah, Daniel, Habakkuk, beginning at Judges 8:15. The surrounding contexts include wilderness.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to יָעַף (H3286) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: יָעַף (yâʻaph) / H3286 is traced through Judges 8:15, Isaiah 40:28, Isaiah 40:30, Isaiah 40:31 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.short: to tire (as if from wearisome flight )
definitions.full: H3286. yaeph I. [ יָעֵף ] verb be weary, faint (Arabic run and shew weariness ) — Qal Perfect וְיָעֵ֑פוּ consecutive Jer 51:58 , 64 ; Imperfect יִיעַף Isa 40:28 ; וַיִּעָ֑ף 44:12 ; יִָֽעֲפוּ 40:30 ; יִיעָ֑פוּ 40:31 ; Jer 2:24 ; יִעָ֑פוּ Hab 2:13 ; — be or grow weary Jer 2:24 (in seeking); = exhaust onself fruitlessly Hab 2:13 (|| יגע ), hence Jer 51:58 , 64 (repeated by error from 51:58 ); of ׳י (negative) Isa 40:28 (|| יגע ); youth 40:30 (|| id. ); the god-fearing 40:31 (|| id. ); be faint from lack of water 44:12 (|| כֹּחַ אֵין from hunger). Hoph`al Participle wearied Dan 9:21 בִּיעָף מֻעָף (see יְעָף ).

occurrences.englishText: He came to the men of Succoth, and said, “See Zebah and Zalmunna, concerning whom you taunted me, saying, ‘Are the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna now in your hand, that we should give bread to your men who are weary?’ ”
Even the youths faint and get weary,
but those who wait for Yahweh will renew their strength.
a wild donkey used to the wilderness, that sniffs the wind in her craving.
Then you shall say, ‘Thus will Babylon sink, and will not rise again because of the evil that I will bring on her; and they will be weary.’ ”
yes, while I was speaking in prayer, the man Gabriel, whom I had seen in the vision at the beginning, being caused to fly swiftly, touched me about the time of the evening offering.
Behold, isn’t it of Yahweh of Armies that the peoples labor for the fire, and the nations weary themselves for vanity?
